newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end feebly, but well off lows.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end feebly, but well off lows.

text.p: Tokyo stocks ended feebly on Thursday but well off their lows as cautious market participants waited for the December futures and options settlement on Friday, brokers said. They said Wall Street's sharp sell-off overnight dampened sentiment.
The Nikkei 225 closed at 20,501.20, down 67.18 points or 0.33 percent. Its December futures were down 50 points at 20,520.
"The market wants to see how the U.S. markets recover later today and how the settlement goes tomorrow," Yasuo Ueki, Nikko Securities general manager said.

Oriental Land's main shareholder, Keisei Electric Railway Co slipped 34 yen to 826 yen, the second most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange on turnover of 6.58 million shares.
Following Keisei was Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd which slid 50 yen to 2,080 yen.

Yaohan Japan Corp's request that its wholesalers and other suppliers accept a longer time-lag before they are paid battered the share price. It fell 100 yen to 441 yen, the largest percentage loser on the first section.
Takefuji Corp rose for the fourth consecutive day. It stood at 9,030 yen, compared to 8,710 yen on Wednesday in over-the-counter (OTC) trade in late afternoon.
The OTC index was down 3.83 points or 0.28 percent at 1,385.63 in late Tokyo trade.

On a sector basis, transport equipment, credit/lease, miscellaneous manufacturers, non-ferrous metals and machinery lead the pack of gainers. Real estate, insurance, land transport, securities and shipbuilding headed the losers.
